children: Surf Air Mobility's third-quarter revenue rose 25% year over year, while its net loss narrowed 25%. Higher on-demand charter revenue, driven by larger-jet sales and more charter flights, more than offset lower scheduled revenue following the exit of certain EAS routes; lower other expense also helped narrow the loss.
¹ Reported as “Revenue”. ² Reported as “Net loss”. ³ Reported as “Net loss per share applicable to common shareholders, basic and diluted”.
: Revenue increased 121% to $19.0M, driven by larger-jet charter sales and an increase in charter flights.
: Revenue decreased 15% to $17.4M, primarily after the company exited certain EAS routes; higher productivity partly offset the decline.
: Cost of revenue rose 21% to $33.5M, as on-demand costs increased with higher revenue and scheduled costs declined with fewer block hours.
: Technology and development expense fell 39% to $1.4M, reflecting higher capitalization of costs related to the platform.
: The company said it is implementing operational improvements and stringent operating expense management to improve airline profitability.
